units.cando: Can say hello and goodbye, say their name and where they are from, and ask how someone is.
grammar: be: I am / you are; Are you …? Yes, I am.
What's your name? / How are you? / Where are you from?
lessons: Hello, I'm …
say hello and say your name
Hello! I'm … / My name is … / Nice to meet you.
Good Morning!
greet people in the morning, afternoon, evening and at night
Good morning! / Good afternoon! / Good evening! / Good night!
How Are You?
ask how someone is and say how you are
How are you? I'm fine, thank you. / Are you happy? Yes, I am.
Where Are You From?
say where you are from and ask a new friend
Where are you from? I'm from … / … is beautiful, too.
Hello on the Phone
say hello and goodbye on the phone
Hello! It's me, … / Bye! / See you! / Take care!
Meet a New Friend
meet a new friend: say hello, introduce yourself and say goodbye
Hi! I'm … What's your name? / I'm from … / Nice to meet you. / See you!

units.cando: Can say who people in their family and their friends are.
lessons: This Is My Family
show your family and say who they are
This is my mum. / This is my dad. / He's … / She's …
Grandma and Grandpa
say who your grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins are
He's my grandpa. / She's my aunt. / Who's that man?
Who's This?
ask 'Who's this?' and say who people are in photos
Who's this? / He's my … / She's my … / It's me!
My Friends
say who your friends are
He's my friend. / She's my best friend. / He's funny.
Eid With My Family
say Eid Mubarak and say who your family are at Eid
Eid Mubarak! / This is my little brother. / She's my big sister.
My Family Tree
show your family tree and say who everyone is
This is me. / This is my … / He's my … / She's my …

units.cando: Can name toys and things and say their colour and size.
grammar: adjective + noun: a red ball, a big blue car
lessons: My Favourite Colour
name colours and say what colour things are
What colour is it? It's red. / It's a red car.
My Toys
name toys and say what they are
What's this? It's a robot. / Is it a car? Yes, it is.
A or An?
name things with 'a' and 'an'
It's a banana. / It's an apple. / It's an egg.
Big and Small
describe toys with big, small, new, old, long and beautiful
It's a big car. / It's a small red ball. / It's old.
At the Toy Shop
name and describe toys in a toy shop
What's that? It's a plane. / Look at that bike!
Show and Tell
show your favourite toy and describe it
My favourite toy is a … / It's a small white teddy bear.

units.cando: Can count to 20, say how old they are and ask and answer 'How many …?'.
grammar: How old are you? I'm seven (years old). / How old is he? He's …
lessons: Count to Ten
count from one to ten and say your favourite number
One, two, three … ten! / My favourite number is …
How Old Are You?
ask and say how old people are
How old are you? I'm seven (years old). / How old is he? He's one.
Happy Birthday!
say happy birthday and ask how old someone is today
Happy birthday! / How old are you today? I'm eight today!
How Many?
ask and answer 'How many …?' about things in your classroom
How many pencils? Six pencils. / How many books? Four.
Eleven to Twenty
count from eleven to twenty and talk about players' numbers
He's number twelve. / Eleven players. / He's fifteen.
My Birthday Party
plan a birthday party with numbers and ages
How old is she? She's five. / How many balloons? Five balloons.

Say 'It's a …' and a toy or a thing.

In Mexico, children break a piñata full of sweets.
In China, some people eat long noodles on their birthday.

Who comes to your birthday party?

you write and draw with it
it has pages; you read it
you sit on it
you look out of it; it's in the wall
you carry your books in it

prompts.q: Now you ask me a question!

In Finland, many children start school at seven.
In many countries, children wear a school uniform.
qs: How many children are in your class?
How many books are in your bag?

3-3.exit: Ask me one 'How many …?' question and answer one.

a person in a game or sport

No, he's number fifteen. He's my cousin!

The 2034 World Cup is in Saudi Arabia.

Say two numbers, like 'Ten balloons and one cake.'

Saudi families often give guests dates and Arabic coffee.
Kabsa is popular at big family parties.

How many friends do you want at your party?

dialogue.t: Hi, Faisal! My name is Sam.

grammar.title: I'm … / My name is …
grammar.ar: نقول I'm أو My name is لنقول اسمنا.

dialogue.t: Yes, I am. See you, Dad!

grammar.title: Good morning / afternoon / evening / night
grammar.ar: نقول Good morning صباحاً، وGood afternoon بعد الظهر، وGood evening مساءً، وGood night عند النوم.

words.ex: I'm happy with my new bike.
Are you sad, Ali? Oh no!

dialogue.t: I'm fine, thank you. How are you?
Yes, I am. I'm very happy.

grammar.title: be: I am / you are
grammar.ar: I'm = I am وYou're = You are. وللسؤال نقول Are you …? ونجيب Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
examples: Are you sad? No, I'm not.

dialogue.t: I'm from England. I'm from London.
Yes, it is. Jeddah is beautiful, too!

grammar.title: Where are you from? I'm from …
grammar.ar: نسأل Where are you from? ونجيب I'm from + اسم البلد أو المدينة.

words.ex: I'm on the phone with Grandma.

dialogue.t: I'm fine, thank you. How are you?
Bye, Grandma! See you on Friday!

grammar.title: On the phone: It's me, … / Bye! / See you!
grammar.ar: على الهاتف نقول It's me + اسمنا، ونودّع بـ Bye أو See you أو Take care.

words.ex: Hi! I'm Ali. What's your name?

dialogue.t: Hi! I'm Ali. What's your name?
Hello, Ali! My name is Tom.

grammar.title: Introducing yourself
grammar.ar: نعرّف بأنفسنا: Hello + I'm / My name is + I'm from.

words.ex: This is my mum. She's very kind.
This is my dad. He's tall.
I'm at home with my brother.

dialogue.t: Yes, it is. This is my mum.

grammar.title: This is my …
grammar.ar: نستخدم This is my لنعرّف بشخص من عائلتنا.

words.ex: This is my grandma. She's kind.
My grandpa is in the garden.

words.ar: ابن أو بنت العم أو الخال

dialogue.t: Who's that man in the garden?

grammar.title: He's … / She's …
grammar.ar: نستخدم He's للولد أو الرجل، وShe's للبنت أو المرأة.

words.ex: The baby is my little brother.

grammar.title: Who's this? He's … / She's …
grammar.ar: نسأل Who's this? ونجيب He's my… للولد أو الرجل، وShe's my… للبنت أو المرأة.
examples: Who's this girl? She's my sister.

grammar.title: He's my friend. / She's nice.
grammar.ar: نستخدم He's / She's + اسم أو صفة لنتحدث عن أصدقائنا.

words.ex: This is my little brother, Saad.
This is my big sister, Noura.
My family is at Grandpa's house.

dialogue.t: This is my little brother, Saad.
Great! Who's that man with Grandma?
He's my dad. He's your uncle!

grammar.title: my little brother / my big sister
grammar.ar: نضع little أو big قبل brother أو sister لنقول الأصغر أو الأكبر.

words.ex: This is a photo of my cousin.
This is my brother, and this is me.

words.ar: ابن أو بنت العم أو الخال

dialogue.t: Noura, is this your family tree?
He's my dad. And this is my mum.
This is my grandpa, and this is my grandma.
Is this a photo of your cousin?

grammar.title: This is … / He's … / She's …
grammar.ar: نستخدم This is للتعريف، وHe's / She's لنقول من هو الشخص.

dialogue.t: And is that a black cat?
Yes, it is. And this is a white bird.

grammar.title: What colour is it? It's red.
grammar.ar: نسأل What colour is it? ونجيب It's + اللون. واللون يأتي قبل الاسم: a red car.
examples: What colour is it? It's green.

words.ex: My kite is red and yellow.

dialogue.t: It's a doll. It's my sister's doll.

grammar.title: What's this? It's a …
grammar.ar: نسأل What's this? ونجيب It's a + اسم الشيء.
examples: Is it a kite? Yes, it is.

words.ex: It's an elephant. It's very big.

dialogue.t: And this is an ice cream!

grammar.title: a or an
grammar.ar: نستخدم an قبل الكلمة التي تبدأ بصوت a أو e أو i أو o أو u، ونستخدم a قبل باقي الكلمات.

dialogue.t: Yes. And this is my new car.

grammar.title: adjective + noun: a big blue car
grammar.ar: الصفة تأتي قبل الاسم: a big car. ونقول الحجم ثم اللون: a big red ball.

words.ex: The toy shop is in the mall.

dialogue.t: Look, Ali! It's a big toy shop!
It's a plane. It's white and blue.
It's a green bike. It's beautiful.
It's a teddy bear. It's brown.

grammar.title: What's this? / What's that?
grammar.ar: نستخدم this للشيء القريب وthat للشيء البعيد: What's that? It's a plane.

words.ex: For Show and Tell, this is my robot.
My favourite toy is a kite.
It's soft. It's a teddy bear.

dialogue.t: It's my favourite toy. It's a teddy bear.
It's white. It's a soft white teddy bear.

grammar.title: It's a + size + colour + toy
grammar.ar: نصف اللعبة هكذا: It's a + الحجم + اللون + الاسم.
examples: My favourite toy is a robot.
It's a small white teddy bear.

dialogue.t: Two dates: one for you and one for me!

grammar.title: Numbers 1–10
grammar.ar: نعدّ: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

dialogue.t: Hi! I'm Emma. How old are you?

grammar.title: How old are you? I'm seven.
grammar.ar: نسأل How old are you? ونجيب I'm + العمر، ويمكن أن نضيف years old.
examples: How old is he? He's one.

words.ex: The party is at Faisal's house.

dialogue.t: It's a chocolate cake. Count the candles!

grammar.title: How old is he? He's eight.
grammar.ar: نسأل عن عمر شخص آخر: How old is he? / How old is she? ونجيب He's أو She's + العمر.

grammar.title: How many …? + plural -s
grammar.ar: نسأل How many + الاسم بالجمع (نضيف s): How many books? Four books.

words.ex: My favourite player is number twelve.
My favourite team is Al Hilal.

dialogue.t: Look at the players! How many?
No, he's number fifteen. He's my cousin!

grammar.title: Numbers 11–20
grammar.ar: الأرقام من 11 إلى 20: eleven, twelve, thirteen … twenty. الأرقام من 13 إلى 19 تنتهي بـ teen.

dialogue.t: Eleven plates: ten friends and Lina.

grammar.title: How many …? / How old …?
grammar.ar: How many للسؤال عن العدد، وHow old للسؤال عن العمر.
examples: How old is she? She's five.

stories.title: The Red Ball and the Tall Tree

pages.text: Omar has a new ball. It is red!
Omar kicks the ball. It goes up into the tree!
Omar is sad. "Where is my ball?"
Grandpa comes. "I can help!"
Grandpa is very tall. He gets the ball!
Now they play football. "Goal, Grandpa!"

questions.q: Why can Grandpa get the ball?

pages.text: "Where is my red hat?" asks Sara. It is not on her bed.
Sara looks under the table. "Look! Small feet on the floor!"
"Is it a mouse?" asks her brother Omar. "No, the feet are big," says Sara.
Sara and Omar go to the garden. They hear, "Meow, meow!"
The red hat is in a box. A white cat is in the hat!
Two baby cats sleep with her. Sara smiles. "OK, cat. My hat is your bed now!"

questions.q: Where does Sara see small feet?
Why does Sara say, "My hat is your bed now"?
options: She is angry with the cat.
She is kind and lets the cats keep the hat.
She does not like her hat.

pages.text: Omar has a red kite. It flies up, up, up!
Whoosh! Now the kite is in a tall tree.
"Oh no! My kite!" says Omar.
His friend Sami runs to him. "I can help you!"
Sami has a long stick. One, two, three... the kite comes down!
"Thank you, Sami! Let's fly it together!"

questions.q: Where is the kite after the wind?
Sami has a long stick. What is a stick?
How does Omar feel at the end?

pages.text: Sara has a red magnet. It can pull a spoon!
Oh no! Grandpa's key is in the sand.
Sara looks and looks. She can't see the key.
Sara has an idea. She moves the magnet over the sand.
Click! The key jumps to the magnet!
"Thank you, Sara!" says Grandpa. "You are a scientist!"

options: A good plan in your head

questions.q: Why does Grandpa say "You are a scientist"?
options: Sara uses science to find the key

pages.text: Sara and Grandpa are in the desert. The sand is yellow and hot.
"Look, Grandpa! Small feet in the sand!"
"Is it a cat? Is it a dog?" "No, Sara. Look!"
It is a baby camel. It is sad.
"Come, little camel. Let's find your mum!"
The baby camel runs to its big mum. Now they are happy!

questions.q: Who is with Sara in the desert?
What does Sara see in the sand?
Why is the baby camel happy at the end?

pages.text: "Omar, where are my glasses?" Grandpa asks.
Omar looks under the bed. No glasses, just the cat!
Omar looks in the box. No glasses, just a ball!
Grandpa looks on the table. "Is that my glasses?" "No, Grandpa, it's an apple!"
Then Omar laughs and laughs. "Grandpa, look! They are on your head!"
Grandpa puts on his glasses and smiles. "Now I can see you, Omar. Thank you!"

options: The glasses are on Grandpa's head

pages.text: Omar and Dad are on a boat. The sea is big and blue.
"Look, Dad! What is that?" "It is a turtle, Omar."
The turtle is sad. A bag is on its leg.
"I can help!" says Omar. He takes the bag off.
The turtle is happy now. It swims fast!
"Goodbye, turtle!" Omar puts the bag in the bin.

questions.q: What is on the turtle's leg?
Why is the turtle happy at the end?

pages.text: Omar's kite is in the tree. Oh no, it is very high!
Omar has an idea. "I can make a long arm!"
He gets a long stick and a big spoon. He puts them together.
"Look, Dad! My long arm!" "Wow, Omar! Good job!"
Omar lifts the long arm. Up, up, up!
Now the kite is in his hands. "Let's fly it again, Dad!"

questions.q: What does Omar use to make the long arm?
What does "high" mean in the story?
How does Dad feel about the long arm?
Why does Omar make a long arm?

pages.text: Sara has a big red bag. "Let's go!" says Grandpa.
They are on a fast train. Sara looks out of the window.
"Look, Grandpa! Three camels!" says Sara.
Now Sara can see blue water. "Is that the sea?"
"Yes! We are at the beach," says Grandpa.
Sara opens her bag. "Two kites! One for you, Grandpa!"

questions.q: How do Sara and Grandpa travel?
What does Sara see from the window?
Why does Sara have two kites?

pages.text: This is Sami. He likes football.
Sami kicks the ball. It goes up, up, up!
"I can't kick," says Sami. He is sad.
"You can catch!" says his brother, Omar.
Now Sami is in the goal. He catches the ball!
"Well done, Sami!" says the team. Sami is happy.

options: to take the ball with your hands

pages.text: Omar has a new robot. Its name is Zip.
Zip can walk. Zip can jump and turn!
"Oh no! Where is my cat?" says Omar.
Zip goes under the bed. Beep! Beep!
Here is the cat! "Thank you, Zip!" says Omar.
Now the cat sits on Zip. They are best friends.

questions.q: Why does Omar say "Thank you, Zip!"?

pages.text: Sara and Grandpa go to the museum. It is very big!
"Look, Grandpa! An old cup." "Yes, Sara. It is brown and very old."
"Look! An old door. It is big and blue."
"Look, Grandpa! A photo of a boy and a camel."
Grandpa smiles. "Sara, that boy is me!"
Sara is happy. "Grandpa, you are in the museum!"

questions.q: Where do Sara and Grandpa go?
What color is the old door?
Why is Sara happy at the end?
options: Her grandpa is in the old photo

pages.text: Omar and Dad are in the desert. The sand is hot and yellow.
"Look, Dad! A big gray cloud!" says Omar.
Drip, drip, drip! "It is rain!" Omar laughs.
Now the sun is back. "Dad, where is the rain?"
"Look down, Omar," says Dad. "Small green plants!"
Now there are red, white and yellow flowers! The desert is happy, and Omar is happy too.

questions.q: Who is with Omar in the desert?
What does Omar see in the sky?
Why are there plants and flowers in the desert?

pages.text: Lina and Dad are in the kitchen. "Let's make a pancake!" says Dad.
Lina has eggs and milk. Dad has a big bowl.
Mix, mix, mix! Dad cooks a round, yellow pancake.
Lina puts two dates on the pancake. "Look, eyes!"
Now she puts a red strawberry on it. It is a big smile!
Dad laughs. "Who is it?" "It's you, Dad!" says Lina.

questions.q: Who is in the kitchen with Lina?
What does Lina put on the pancake for eyes?
The pancake is "round". What shape is it?

options: The pancake face looks like him.

pages.text: This is Omar. He has a small red drum.
Boom! Boom! Omar plays his drum. It is very loud!
Oh no! Baby Sara is crying. Mum is sad.
Omar looks at his drum. "I can play soft," he says.
Tap, tap, tap. Sara looks at Omar. She stops crying.
Now Sara is happy. She claps her hands! "Good boy, Omar!" says Mum.

questions.q: "Boom! Boom!" is very loud. What is the opposite of loud?

options: Omar plays his drum very loud.

questions.q: Sara claps her hands. How does she feel?

pages.text: I am Omar. I am a detective!
Oh no! Where is my red ball?
It is not under the bed. It is not in the box.
Look! Small cat feet on the floor.
I go to the garden. The cat has my ball!
Ha ha! The cat and I play with the ball.

questions.q: How does Omar know the cat has the ball?
options: He sees cat feet on the floor
The ball is in the box

stories.title: Super Sami and the Little Cat

pages.text: I am Super Sami! Look at my red cape.
Oh no! A little cat is in the tree.
"I can fly!" says Sami. He jumps and jumps, but he can't fly!
"Dad! Please help!" Dad is very tall.
Dad gets the cat. Now the cat is happy.
Sami gives Dad a blue cape. "Now we are two superheroes!"

questions.q: Dad is very tall. What does "tall" mean?
Why does Sami give Dad a cape?

pages.text: We are in the desert. This is our big green tent.
Mum makes tea. My brother and I sit by the fire.
Look up! I can see the moon and many stars.
Shh! What is that sound? Something is behind the tent.
Dad has a torch. I can see two big eyes!
It is a baby camel! "Good night, little camel," I say.

questions.q: How does the child feel at the end?

pages.text: Miss Huda has a big box. "What's in the box?" asks Omar.
Tap, tap! The box moves!
"Is it a ball? Is it a cat?" asks Lina.
"No!" says Miss Huda. She opens the box.
It's a little green turtle! The turtle is very slow.
"His name is Rocket!" says Omar. Everyone laughs.

options: A rocket is fast, but the turtle is slow.

pages.text: Knock, knock! "Who is at the door?" asks Sara.
"Is it Dad?" "No. Dad is in the kitchen."
"Is it my brother, Ali?" "No. Ali is in the garden."
"Is it Mum?" "No! I am here," says Mum with a smile.
Sara opens the door. It is Grandma, with a big red bag!
"Hello! A cake for my family!" says Grandma. Everyone is happy.

questions.q: What do we do in a kitchen?
Why is everyone happy at the end?
options: Grandma is here with a cake

stories.title: Ring, Ring! Where Is the Phone?

pages.text: Grandpa can't find his phone. "Where is it?" he asks.
Sara looks in his bag. No phone!
Sara has an idea. "I can call it, Grandpa!"
Sara takes Mum's phone. Ring, ring!
The sound is in the cat's bed! The cat is sitting on the phone.
Grandpa laughs. "Thank you, Sara! You are very clever!"

questions.q: Why does Grandpa say "You are very clever"?
options: Sara finds the phone with a good idea.

pages.text: This is Al-Jazari. He likes to make things.
Look! A big elephant. It is a clock!
There is water in the elephant. Drip, drip, drip.
A bird sings. A man hits a drum. Boom!
"What time is it?" asks a boy. "Look at the elephant!" says Al-Jazari.
"I want to make things too!" says the boy. Al-Jazari smiles.

questions.q: What does Al-Jazari like to do?
How does the boy feel at the end?

pages.text: It is hot. The sun is big and yellow.
"Dad, look! My little plant is sad."
"Look, Sara! Big grey clouds!" says Dad.
"Rain! Rain!" Sara and Dad run outside.
"Drink, little plant!" says Sara.
Now the sun is back. Look, a red flower!

questions.q: What comes after the grey clouds?
What does the plant have at the end?

pages.text: Sara has a big paper. She wants to paint a tree.
"Oh no! I have only blue," says Sara.
Her brother Omar comes. "I have yellow!" he says.
Sara mixes blue and yellow. "Look! It is green!"
Sara paints a green tree. Omar paints a yellow sun.
Mum looks at the picture. "Wow! You paint well together!"

questions.q: What does Sara want to paint?
Why is Sara sad at first?

pages.text: Huda finds an old clock. It is Grandpa Saleh's clock.
She turns it. Tick, tock... Whoosh!
Now Huda is in a small house. A little boy has a red ball.
"I am Saleh," says the boy. "Let's play!"
Huda turns the clock again. Whoosh! She is home.
Grandpa holds an old red ball and smiles. "Thank you for the game, Huda!"

questions.q: Who is the little boy in the small house?
Where is Huda at the end of the story?

pages.text: Sara and Omar are at the beach. The sea is blue.
"Look! A bottle!" says Omar. A small red crab is in it.
The crab can't get out. "Help it, please!" says Sara.
Omar opens the bottle. The crab walks out!
The crab runs to the sea. "Bye, crab!" says Sara.
Omar puts the bottle in the bin. "A clean beach is a happy beach!"

questions.q: Why does Omar put the bottle in the bin?
options: To give it to the crab

pages.text: Look! It is raining. Ali has a big yellow umbrella.
His friend Sami is sad. "I have no umbrella."
Ali smiles. "Come here, Sami!"
Now two boys are under the umbrella.
Look! A little cat is wet. "Come here, little cat!"
Two happy boys and one happy cat. It is a big umbrella and a big heart!

questions.q: What does "wet" mean in the story?
options: Full of water from the rain

questions.q: Who is under the umbrella at the end?
What kind of boy is Ali?

pages.text: "Look, Dad! A baby camel!" says Omar. It is in the sand.
"It is sad," says Huda. "Where is its mother?"
They walk up a big hill. The sun is very hot.
"I can see camels!" says Omar. "One, two, three!"
The baby camel runs to its mother. Now it is happy!
"Thank you!" says the camel man. Omar and Huda smile.

questions.q: What do Omar and Dad see in the sand?
How many camels can Omar see on the hill?
What does "hot" mean in "The sun is very hot"?
Why is the camel man happy at the end?
options: The baby camel is back with its mother

pages.text: "Dad, look! What is in the box?" asks Omar.
"It has four legs," says Dad. "Is it a cat?" asks Omar.
"No. It is green. It is very slow."
"Is it a frog?" "No. Frogs jump!"

"His name is Speedy," says Dad. Omar laughs.

pages.text: Omar and Dad sit on the roof. It is night.
"Look, Dad! The moon is big and white."
Omar counts the stars. "One, two, three... I can see ten!"
"Dad, that star is red." Dad smiles. "That is not a star."
"It is Mars, Omar. Mars is a planet."
"Hello, Mars! One day, I can fly to you!"
